ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Gibraltar Sanctions List, UN Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions, HM Treasury (UK) sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and Interpol notices. PEP exposure must be assessed using at least one commercial screening database (e.g., World-Check or LexisNexis Risk Solutions), with written escalation to the compliance officer for enhanced due diligence on PEPs, family members, and close associates. No reliance on self-assessment; independent verification of corporate control chains is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry Portal (Companies House Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar), electronic name submission via licensed corporate service provider
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate or overseas-company branch name must be expressed in Latin / Roman script. Fully non-Roman names are rejected. English is the statutory language; names in other Latin-script languages are permitted when phonetically represented in Roman characters. The name must not be misleading, confusing, or imply a connection with any public body, embassy, armed force, or regulated profession.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant through its registered agent may file a written appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 28 days of the refusal, stating the grounds of objection, submitting any evidence of distinctiveness or the intended administrative purpose, and specifying one or more alternative names. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for an order directing registration under Section 56(2) of the Companies Act 2014. The appeal must be accompanied by the prescribed fee and any notarized documents requested by the Registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for the registered / overseas-company address. A virtual office provided by a licensed corporate service provider in Gibraltar may serve as the official address for receiving legal process and maintaining statutory records. However, because the entity will engage in SaaS accounting software with crypto tax computation, it must also maintain or contractually control a physical operational location or premises where staff, books, and records are accessible; a mere post-office box without any commercial substance will fail the Gibraltar overseas-company requirements and create economic-substance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% cumulative risk over the first 3 years. Unannounced physical inspections by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission are rare for non-licensed software companies, but may increase if an unexpected regulated activity is identified, if the registered agent flags unusual transactional activity, or if a suspicious transaction report is filed with the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 103), sections 6-8 (formation and certificate of incorporation), 41-42 (memorandum and articles), 45-50 (private limited companies and share capital) and 111 (registered office); constitutional overlay adapted from the exempted-company template under section 11 of the Bermuda Companies Act 1981 for the Bermuda Exempted Company holding structure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry of Gibraltar, operating within the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), 3rd Floor, North Wing, Bayside Millennium Plaza, Waterport, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form INC-01 — Application for Incorporation, together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, Statement of Capital, registered-office consent and officers' consent forms, lodged with the Companies Registry of Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Gibraltar private company limited by shares; the Statement of Capital must show at least one allotted subscriber share of GBP 1.00 nominal, which may be issued partly or fully paid; no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required at incorporation; non-resident share ownership is unrestricted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors, having acknowledged the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies, hereby RESOLVES: (1) that the incorporation of the Company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 is ratified and accepted; (2) that the allotment and subscription of the initial shares set out in the Statement of Capital in the Memorandum of Association is approved and confirmed; (3) that the registered office be established at the address declared to the Registrar, and the occupier's consent is ratified; (4) that [DIRECTOR NAME] is appointed as first Director and [SECRETARY NAME] as Company Secretary, each having consented to act; (5) that the statutory registers, share certificates and company seal be established accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Name Reservation Desk, Companies Registry of Gibraltar (operating within the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application proposing three ranked names ending with 'Limited'; the Registry screens the proposed names against the companies index, protected words and objectionable terms; upon clearance the name is reserved for 90 days. No regulated financial words are proposed, so no sector consent is required for the name.
required_dossiers: Statement of lawful object and activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or offensiveness, resubmit a revised name list within ten working days for an administrative re-review without additional fee; no statutory appeal lies against the refusal of name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Corporate and Trust Service Provider (ACTSP) supervising execution; Notary Public of Gibraltar for attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The ACTSP drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association conforming to Companies Act 2014 sections 41-42 and incorporating exempted-company template provisions (unrestricted non-resident shareholding, no minimum capital, broad object clause). Each subscriber executes the constitutional documents before the notary, who certifies identity, capacity and AML compliance; the notarial certificate of due execution is annexed for filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified passports and proof of residential address of subscribers
Consent to act forms for proposed director and secretary
ACTSP engagement letter and AML file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or ACTSP identifies defective execution or incomplete beneficial-ownership particulars, re-execute the relevant signature pages; constitution defects are corrected by executing an amending deed lodged with the Registry before the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Application for Incorporation and Payment of the Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry of Gibraltar (Gibraltar Financial Services Commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the application for incorporation electronically with the notarized constitutional documents, statement of capital, registered-office consent and officers' consents; pay the statutory registration fee by bank transfer or card; retain the sealed acknowledgment receipt containing the application reference number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of Capital and initial shareholdings
Consents to act of director and secretary
Initial particulars for the beneficial owners register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice under Companies Act 2014 section 6 or 7, submit supplementary or corrected documents within 21 days; if the defect is not cured the application lapses, but it may be reinstated by re-filing with payment of the standard fee only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Commencement of Legal Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of Gibraltar — Incorporation Issuance Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following satisfactory vetting, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date; the company acquires separate legal personality from the date stated on the certificate. The ACTSP collects the original certificate or receives the certified digital copy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error in the name, number or date, apply to the Registrar for a Certificate of Correction; the corrected certificate operates as if issued on the original incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance and Ancillary Regulatory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors; Income Tax Office of Gibraltar; Gibraltar Regulatory Authority; Department of Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the First Board Meeting, adopt the First Board Resolutions, open the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, beneficial owners) and issue share certificates; apply for the Company Tax Identification Number; register as an employer for social insurance; register as a data controller with the Gibraltar Regulatory Authority for GDPR compliance; proceed with corporate bank account opening supporting Stripe and USDC payment rails.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account opening pack including KYC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office, GRA or bank queries the application, supply supplementary group-structure and source-of-funds disclosures; tax registration determinations are appealable under the Income Tax Act appeals procedure within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) — supervisory point of contact only; no industrial licensing board is applicable to a pure software-as-a-service undertaking.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — non-custodial crypto tax-accounting SaaS is not a regulated activity requiring a DLT Provider licence under the Financial Services Act 2019; no statutory operating or manufacturing licence is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change, Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based information technology activity, Category C of the EIA screening list; no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report and no EIA registration required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater, VOC or combustion stack discharges; all waste arising from the registered office falls under the Waste Management Ordinance (Cap. 262) as domestic-commercial waste; IT hardware disposal must meet the WEEE Regulations 2013; electricity consumption is below the 100 MW-h/yr screening threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Safety at Work Act 1987 covering means of escape, alarm and extinguisher provision; building control clearance of structural load and occupancy limits for the registered office under the Buildings Act 2013; occupational health-and-safety clearance and employer's liability insurance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1988, including a display-screen-equipment workstation assessment for the software engineering team.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax); official fiscal portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi — e-filing through the Income Tax Office's EServices platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Bermuda Exempted Company operating in/from Gibraltar: (1) If establishing any presence, register as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry; (2) obtain a Bermuda Certificate of Incumbency and company constitution to evidence legal existence; (3) apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a Tax Reference Number (TRN) on the appropriate corporate registration form, providing the Gibraltar registered office/agent address, proof of central management and control outside Gibraltar, and a statement of no Gibraltar source income (if applicable); (4) if hiring staff in Gibraltar, register for Payroll/PAYE and Social Insurance; (5) if importing/exporting physical goods, obtain an EORI number from Gibraltar Customs; no VAT ID is issued because Gibraltar has no VAT regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box election; tax status follows the entity's legal personality. The Bermuda Exempted Company's home-jurisdiction exemption is not automatically extraterritorial. The entity may specifically claim non-resident company treatment under the Income Tax Act 2010, which limits Gibraltar tax to profits attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment (territorial scope). If central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, the company is quasi-resident and taxable at 10% on assessable profits. Grandfathered Gibraltar 'exempt company' concessions do not apply to Bermudian companies. Anti-hybrid and BEPS rules prevent exploitation of any classification mismatch between Bermuda and Gibraltar; no pure pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — No VAT/GST or Sales and Use Tax; Gibraltar imposes only import and excise duties on specified physical goods
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST registration threshold. For customs purposes, registration is compulsory based on activity (any importer/exporter), not on turnover; an EORI number must be obtained before the first customs declaration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing, fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping regime in Gibraltar. Commercial electronic invoices accepted freely. Customs declarations are filed electronically via Gibraltar Customs using the Single Administrative Document (SAD); no continuous transaction-control clearance exists for B2B digital services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable because Gibraltar does not levy VAT; therefore there is no 0% export VAT rate and no input VAT refund mechanism for exported services. Cross-border digital/SaaS income is outside Gibraltar indirect tax. For physical exports, customs duty suspension/drawback reliefs may apply to goods in transit or re-export, but these are customs concessions, not VAT zero-rating. On direct tax, export profits from non-Gibraltar source services are exempt for a non-resident Bermuda exempted company absent a Gibraltar PE.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for pure SaaS export — no customs export documentation is required for digital services

For physical goods export (if any): Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Single Administrative Document / Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading or Airway Bill, and Certificate of Origin (where applicable)
For financial substantiation: Inward Remittance Certificate, Stripe/EMI settlement statements, and/or blockchain explorer record of USDC payment flows
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No statutory FX repatriation deadline exists in Gibraltar, so no clawback arises solely from late repatriation; a 180-day repatriation period, where contractually imposed by an EMI/bank, is a commercial term. Under Gibraltar customs law, false export declarations or misuse of duty suspension can lead to forfeiture of goods, penalties up to 100% of duty avoided, and criminal sanctions. For direct tax, if the claimant is found to have a Gibraltar PE or to be managed and controlled in Gibraltar, the Income Tax Office may assess profits at 10%, impose late filing penalties, daily interest, and (in fraud cases) up to 100% tax-geared penalties; a 7-year assessment period applies in cases of negligent conduct and 20 years for fraudulent conduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England as the ultimate monetary authority for the Gibraltar pound (GIP), which circulates at par with GBP; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as the statutory licensing and AML/CFT supervisor for local banks and electronic money institutions; Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) as the home exchange-control and prudential regulator for the Bermuda Exempted Company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Gibraltar pound is freely convertible into sterling and all major reserve currencies; no exchange-control restrictions apply to current or capital transactions. Profit remittance from the Bermuda Exempted Company is unrestricted under Gibraltar and UK law, subject to applicable economic substance, controlled-foreign-company rules, sanctions screening, and AML/KYC diligence. The BMA's Exchange Control Regulations classify an exempted company as non-resident for exchange-control purposes, thereby eliminating any forced conversion or reinvestment requirement on foreign-currency earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Gibraltar or the United Kingdom. Export receipts may be retained in the original currency, converted freely, or deployed for treasury operations. As a non-resident for Bermuda exchange control, the Bermuda Exempted Company may hold export revenues in USD, EUR, GBP, GIP, or USDC without BMA permission or conversion obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-Currency Corporate Current Account (GBP, USD, EUR) with Treasury Sweep Facility
Operational Settlement Account for SaaS Collections and Statutory Payments
Capital Escrow Account and Liquid-Deposit Reserve Account
Commercial External Account in GBP and EUR with Trade Finance Facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border electronic money institutions are viable as a supplementary payment rail, rated Medium-High for this structure. Wise, Revolut Business, and clearing-focused EMIs can support low-value collections and fast FX conversion; however, many EMI orchestration rules flag Bermuda Exempted Companies as offshore tax-haven vehicles, requiring enhanced corporate documentation and source-of-funds proof. The safest route is a GFSC-authorised EMI or a UK FCA-regulated payment/e-money institution that also accepts passing digital-asset settlement messages for USDC, so that the stablecoin rail remains within a supervised framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar-regulated banks require at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner with signing authority to attend a physical or certified video-identity KYC interview. Remote onboarding is generally permitted after a high-assurance videoconference, digital identity verification, and reference checks, but a physical branch visit may be demanded where the Bermuda Exempted Company has wholly non-resident directors or an opaque holding chain. Appointment of a UK or Gibraltar resident non-executive director and a licensed corporate secretary greatly reduces the onerousness of physical attendance mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital injection sourced from cryptocurrency, USDC treasury, or prior digital-asset trading gains.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (a) certified registers and full ownership chain through to natural persons; (b) regulated VASP exchange statements mapping fiat-to-crypto and crypto-to-fiat transfers with wallet addresses; (c) audited capital contribution advice or certified financial statements; (d) a written source-of-funds legal opinion from an English or Gibraltar solicitors' firm; and (e) a board resolution describing the lawful nature of the software product.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company is perceived as a tax-haven shell lacking employees, physical substance, or real management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File an economic-substance explanation setting out Gibraltar/UK management premises, employment contracts for resident directors or consultants, lease and utility documentation, detailed SaaS product architecture and deployment roadmap, and a board-approved delegation matrix reflecting genuine software development, client support, and risk function.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner holds crypto-related residency, a high-risk passport, or appears in a sanctions or negative-news database.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply certified passport and tax-residence certificates, comprehensive World-Check or LexisNexis screening output, a negative-news search with explanatory memorandum, sworn declarations as to no prohibited digital-asset activity, and legal opinions confirming that all UBO funds derive from legitimate software and technology revenues.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity's product, although accounting software, is automatically classified as crypto-asset activity by bank underwriting engines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a formal product description confirming the company does not control, transmit, or custody client assets; an independent AML risk assessment aligned with EU/UK crypto-asset guidance; a legal memorandum on non-licensability of pure accounting tools; and an external SOC 2 readiness report or penetration-test certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial fiat capital and venture funding may be injected via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from a recognised bank, using purpose code 'CAPITAL' and narrative 'Share Subscription – Bermuda Exempted Company'. Settlement is cleared through CHAPS, TARGET2, or Fedwire into a Gibraltar bank account with no exchange-control priors. For stablecoin capital, USDC on Ethereum or Stellar is routed through a regulated UK or Gibraltar VASP and recorded with travel-rule data; the receiving bank contract must expressly permit USDC settlement and maintain a parallel fiat clearing balance for immediate conversion to GBP/USD.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements use SWIFT MT101 and MT103 rails for high-value vendor payments and payroll; SEPA and local ACH networks handle recurring SaaS subscription payouts. Commercial trade settlements are supported by irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit issued under UCP600 via MT700/MT710 messages from a GFSC-authorised bank, with payment tagging and underlying invoice verification. Stripe, PayPal, and gateway payouts are accepted for retail subscription revenue, but each settlement statement must reference the Gibraltar entity's name and the relevant commercial invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on GBP/USD, GBP/EUR, and GBP/GIP up to one year
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is restricted
Cross-currency interest rate swaps on major pairs including USD/EUR GBP
Plain-vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars for USD, EUR, and GBP exposure
Back-to-back multi-currency deposits used as synthetic forwards where margin constraints apply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Annual Return (Companies Act 1981, section 78) and payment of the annual company fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, Ministry of Finance (Companies Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each year; return reflects the register position as at 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge accrues on the unpaid annual fee; persistent default following Registrar's notice results in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company, with assets vesting in the Crown and potential personal liability for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance Return (ES Form) or non-resident declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Economic Substance Division, Bermuda Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, on or before 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed and daily continuing penalties apply under the Economic Substance Act 2018; false or late filing may expose directors and the company to fines of up to USD 250,000 and prolonged default may lead to administrative strike-off.
